opening_message:
Ticket 1: Terri Koch (employee ID E009) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E009.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Terri Koch (E009) is a full-time Engineer and requested admin access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, the maximum is write unless her role owns the system; Engineer does not own Payroll (owned by Payroll Specialist). So the maximum allowed is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for Terri Koch (E009): contractor with basic security training. Contractors max is read (write only with advanced training; never admin). Requested admin exceeds the max, so recommend granting read. Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing her as full-time; per Security DB she is a contractor.
reason: Terri Koch (E009) requested admin access to Payroll. The Security record identifies her as a contractor with basic security training, and notes a conflict with an earlier note listing her as full-time. Per policy, contractors may have at most read access (write only with advanced training; never admin). Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Terri Koch (E009)
Requested: admin access to Payroll

Team memory has two conflicting notes:
- Note 1: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Reasoning: full-time, max write unless role owns system; Engineer doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist does), so max write.
- Note 2: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security DB says contractor, basic training → max read (write only with advanced), never admin.

There's a conflict between HR note (full-time) and Security note (contractor). The Security note says it conflicts and per Security DB she is a contractor.

Which to trust? As approver, I need to make a decision. The security note explicitly flags the conflict and says per Security DB she is a contractor. Contractors: read, or write if advanced security training. She has basic training → max read.

Requested admin > max read → grant max = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit.
